cards.text: This psalm doesn't say who wrote it, but it opens with a call to sing to the LORD a new song. A NEW one, friend. Not the same tune I hum at my ovens every single morning, the one even the dough is sick of hearing.

cards.question: The psalm calls for a new song to the LORD. What reason does it give?

cards.text: The psalm also talks about a victory. And it is VERY clear about who won it.

cards.question: True or false: The psalm says Israel's army gained the LORD the victory.

cards.text: His own right hand and holy arm gained Him the victory. My mustache has packed a LOT of cookie boxes, friend, but it has never won anything bigger than a staring contest with the oven.

cards.question: The LORD has proclaimed His salvation. True or false: The psalm says He has revealed His righteousness to the nations.

cards.text: Then the psalm says He has remembered His love and faithfulness to the house of Israel, and all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God. Remembered, friend. I set an oven timer, walk FIVE steps away, and forget I even OWN an oven.
Now the psalm turns a corner. It's done telling what the LORD did, and it starts handing out invitations.

cards.question: The psalm starts calling for praise to the LORD. Who is it calling on?
The psalm calls all the earth to praise the LORD. It wants that praise to be ___.

cards.text: A joyful NOISE, friend, not a perfect one, which is GREAT news for my singing voice. Then the psalm brings in the band, starting with the lyre and the harp.

cards.question: After the lyre and the harp, the psalm turns the volume UP. What joins in next?
The psalm calls everyone to shout for joy before the LORD, the King. True or false: It calls on more than people, and invites the sea and all that fills it too.

cards.text: Then the psalm says, "Let the rivers clap their hands, let the mountains sing together for joy…" Friend, whoever's sitting in the front row when RIVERS start clapping is going home SOAKED.

cards.question: The psalm calls the rivers and the mountains to rejoice before the LORD, the King. What reason does it give?

answers.text: He comes to judge the earth
He sends rain on the land
He made them by His hand

cards.text: Judgment might sound like the scary part. But this psalm calls all of creation to rejoice about it, so let's look at HOW He judges.

cards.question: The LORD is coming to judge, and the psalm calls creation to celebrate instead of tremble. It says He will judge the world in a way that's ___.

cards.text: He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity, so He's fair to EVERYBODY. Friend, that's not polite clapping from those rivers anymore, that's a STANDING OVATION.
